title: Windowed LRU allocator with slot-slicing for paged KV and coordinated prefill scheduling
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Problem: As model serving scales to long-context chat and multi-tenant workloads, our paged KV cache exhibits higher fragmentation and uneven eviction behavior: large pages get partially used, hot prefixes collide with cold ones, and prefill-induced bursts cause tail latency spikes. This ticket introduces a combined allocator + scheduling strategy: 1) slot-slicing (logical subdivision of physical KV pages into finer slots that can be allocated independently to keys/prefixes), 2) a windowed-LRU allocator that maintains a short-term hot window for fast-touch prefixes and a long-term reservoir to avoid premature eviction, and 3) coordinated prefill/decode scheduling to avoid large prefill batches evicting hot slots and to prioritize kernel placement for prefill vs decode phases. Goal: reduce fragmentation, reduce 95th/99th tail latency on decode by 15-25%, and improve effective cache hit-rate for hot prefixes by 10% on conversational workloads.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end change can be enabled via a runtime flag and disabled without restart
Benchmarked 95th token-decode latency decreases by >=15% on conv-demo workload compared to baseline
Measured KV cache logical occupancy (hot-prefix hit-rate) increases by >=10% on long-context traces
No material regression (>2%) in aggregate throughput for mixed small/large-sequence workloads
Unit + integration tests for slot lifecycle, eviction invariants, and scheduler gates are added and green
risks: Increased allocator complexity may add CPU overhead on hot path if slot bookkeeping is not optimized
Slot-slicing could lead to internal fragmentation if slice size poorly matched to typical prefix lengths
Coordination between prefill scheduler and kernel router needs careful backpressure handling to avoid head-of-line blocking
Edge cases when migrating existing pages to sliced representation during rolling upgrade
decisions: Use 4KB as default slot-slice granularity (configurable) based on median prefix KV footprint from tracing
Maintain two LRU lists: a small fast window (target 5-10% of cache) and a long LRU reservoir for aged entries
Eviction policy: prefer evicting cold slices first; if page has mixed cold/hot slices, do intra-page compaction asynchronously
Integrate allocator metadata into page headers to avoid separate global maps and reduce lookup latency
Prefill scheduler exposes soft tokens-per-second budget to kernel router; prefill batches that exceed budget are split across lower-priority lanes
notes: This approach complements previous paged compaction work but focuses on logical subdivision to reduce cross-prefix collisions and faster reclaiming of unused slices. The slot-slicing is intentionally conservative to avoid high bookkeeping cost; we'll iterate after microbenchmarks.
comments: 2025-02-10 Asha K: Created ticket. Collected traces from conv-demo and multi-tenant staging clusters. Observed 22% of pages have <=25% utilized bytes causing effective fragmentation.
2025-02-14 Daniel C: Spike implemented minimal slot metadata in C++ allocator to measure overhead. CPU overhead for 8K requests/sec workload is ~1.8% with 4KB slices.
2025-02-18 Elena M (perf): Microbenchmarks: 95th decode latency improved 18% on baseline for long-context traces with windowed-LRU enabled plus coordinated prefill. Throughput steady within 1.5%.
2025-02-22 Design review (Arman P): Concerned about slice size variability across models; requested config knob and heuristics per-model based on observed KV footprint distribution.
2025-02-25 PR feedback (code review): Added fast-path for completely-hot pages to avoid per-slice locking in the common case; will add tests for concurrent prefill eviction races (PR #4821).

2025-03-01 Ops note (Maya L): Rolling enablement on staging with feature-flag; observed one pod with OOM during migration due to temporary double-allocation — fixed by serializing page-conversion during upgrade.
2025-03-02 Daniel C: Updated ticket with benchmark dashboard links and plan for canary rollout next week.
